lessons.title: Finding Rank from the Other End
lessons.concept: In a row (or ordered list) of N people, a person's position from one end can be converted to position from the other end. This uses the total count and the given rank.
lessons.formula: Rank from other end = Total persons - Rank from given end + 1.
lessons.worked_example: In a class of 40 students, if Ravi is 12th from the top, his rank from the bottom = 40 - 12 + 1 = 29th.
mistakes: Forgetting to add 1 after subtracting from total

lessons.title: Finding Total from Ranks of One Person
lessons.concept: If the same person's rank from both ends is known, the total number of persons can be calculated. The person is counted in both ranks, so 1 is subtracted to avoid double counting.
lessons.formula: Total persons = Rank from left/top + Rank from right/bottom - 1.
lessons.worked_example: If a student is 7th from the left and 9th from the right in a row, total students = 7 + 9 - 1 = 15.
mistakes: Applying the formula when ranks are of different persons
Mixing up positions and counts between people

lessons.title: Finding Number of Persons Between Two
lessons.concept: When positions of two different people are known from the same end in a row of known total, or from opposite ends, you can determine how many people sit between them. Convert positions to the same reference if needed, then compute the gap.
lessons.formula: If positions from same end are p and q (p < q), persons between = q - p - 1. If from opposite ends in total N, convert one rank: position from left of right-end person = N - rank_from_right + 1, then apply same formula.
lessons.worked_example: In a row of 20, A is 4th from left and B is 6th from right. B's position from left = 20 - 6 + 1 = 15. Persons between A(4th) and B(15th) = 15 - 4 - 1 = 10.
mistakes: Not converting both positions to the same end before finding the gap
Assuming the two people are in a particular order without checking

practice.question: In a row of 30 students, a student is 8th from the left. What is the student's position from the right?
practice.explanation: Position from right = Total - Position from left + 1 = 30 - 8 + 1 = 23rd.

practice.question: In a queue, a person is 10th from the front and 15th from the back. How many persons are there in the queue?
practice.explanation: Total = Rank from front + Rank from back - 1 = 10 + 15 - 1 = 24.

practice.question: In a row, Ramesh is 6th from the left and Suresh is 8th from the right. If there are 18 persons in the row, how many persons are between Ramesh and Suresh?
practice.explanation: Suresh's position from left = 18 - 8 + 1 = 11th. Ramesh is 6th from left. Persons between = 11 - 6 - 1 = 4.

questions.explanation: Q's position from left = 16 - 4 + 1 = 13th. Persons between P (3rd) and Q (13th) = 13 - 3 - 1 = 9.

questions.question: In a row, A is 10th from the left and B is 12th from the right. After they interchange positions, A becomes 15th from the left. Total people =?
questions.explanation: After the interchange, A sits at B's old position, which is 12th from the right and (now) 15th from the left. Total = position from left + position from right - 1 = 15 + 12 - 1 = 26.

questions.question: How many persons are between A and B if A is 8th from the left and B is 13th from the left in the same row?
questions.explanation: Persons strictly between two ranks m and n = |n - m| - 1 = 13 - 8 - 1 = 4 (positions 9, 10, 11 and 12 lie between 8 and 13).
